headline: Global Metals Rout Deepens Amid Fed Rate Hike Fears and Dollar Strength
paragraphs: Precious metals suffered historic losses this week, with silver plunging 7.31 percent on the day and 16.22 percent for the week while gold fell 3.98 percent. The broader everything crash was driven by surging US dollar strength and hardening Federal Reserve interest rate hike expectations. Platinum dropped 4.57 percent and palladium retreated 2.59 percent alongside the deepening selloff.

Industrial metals and energy complexes also faced heavy selling pressure. Copper sank 2.84 percent on the day and over ten percent for the week, entering a bear market as fund selling and an unwinding AI-driven rally wreaked havoc on industrial demand. Brent crude fell 2.29 percent due to strong Middle East export flows keeping supply robust, while WTI crude edged up 0.49 percent. In contrast, natural gas surged 16 percent on the day, with an ECB board member warning about second-round inflationary effects as Eurozone inflation hit four percent.
The exchange rate stood at 1.0970 EUR/USD, reflecting a relatively stable euro against a strengthening dollar that amplified domestic commodity costs for Irish businesses.
